StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterModifyingCardPlayCount.rationale: Identical shape and identical reasoning to power/duplication's entry for the same hook -- the decrement is folded into the modifier rather than fired from Hook.ModifyCardPlayCount's notification list (Hook.cs:1376-1384). Equivalent today; kept as a divergence because the machinery is absent rather than unused.

AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: SLOT. AbstractModel.AfterSideTurnEnd is dispatched by Hook.AfterTurnEnd (Hook.cs:1267-1292), called for the player side at CombatManager.cs:1307 -- AFTER the turn-end card effects and the hand flush. The sim's on_player_turn_end is Hook.BeforeTurnEnd (combat.py:654), which runs BEFORE _process_turn_end_cards (combat.py:658) and before the flush (combat.py:661-662); the sim's real AfterTurnEnd slot, after_player_turn_end (combat.py:665), is available and unused. THE CONCRETE ROUTE, which applies to every unit in this group: StampedePower (powers.py:1025-1041) auto-plays Attack cards from ITS on_player_turn_end, i.e. inside the very same dispatch, and _process_turn_end_cards runs more card effects immediately after. So in the game every turn-end auto-play happens while this power is still on the creature, and in the sim whether it does depends on hook-registration order between this power and Stampede. Reproduce the affected population with `py audit/tools/power_census.py slots`. Third-file citations, not hashed here. LIVE for this unit for the same reason as power/duplication's, and more sharply: One-Two Punch doubles ATTACKS specifically and Stampede's turn-end auto-plays are exactly Attack plays, so the two powers are made for each other. In the game the stack is still there for them; in the sim it is a registration-order coin flip. Both are ported Ironclad-pool card powers.

powers.py:972-974 tests CardType.ATTACK and returns the unmodified count otherwise -- and, importantly, returns BEFORE the _tick, so a non-Attack play does not burn a stack. Matches C#, whose AfterModifyingCardPlayCount fires only for listeners that changed the value.
